# Tests the outcome ratchet in ci.yml leaves alone (#1786).
#
# One test id per line, as `scripts/test_outcome_record.py` names a test:
# `<classname>::<name>`, for example
# `tests.test_store.TestOpen::test_readonly[a]`. Copy the id from the step
# summary as it is. `*` matches any run of characters, so
# `tests.test_store.TestOpen::test_readonly[*]` names every parameter of
# that test; every other character, `[` and `?` included, matches itself.
# A test listed here may be skipped, xfailed or never executed without the
# diff calling it a ratchet violation. Say why on a `#` line above each
# entry; a comment after the id on the same line becomes part of the id,
# which then matches nothing.
#
# Two cases need no entry. A new test that is never executed (behind
# `--run-perf`, or a bench-gate test) is not a violation, unless its test
# function lost a test with another outcome. New ids that rename removed ids
# of one test function, as a pytest upgrade does to parameter ids, are not
# violations when both hold the same outcomes the same number of times.
# Every other new skip
# needs an entry, a platform skip included: the ratchet reads the outcome,
# never the skip reason.

# Windows-only (#1833): `skipif(not WIN32)`, so both Linux legs skip them.
tests.test_core_gate_background_windows_1761::test_a_cmd_shim_receives_the_argv_intact
tests.test_core_gate_background_windows_1761::test_the_detached_child_runs_the_stub_on_windows
